title: Flying Officer P Pease
memorial_details: description: Flying Officer A. Peter Pease / Royal Air Force Volunteer Reserve // (image) / Eldest son of Sir Richard and Lady Pease / Born in London 15 February 1918 / Raised in Richmond, Yorkshire / Educated at Eton College and Trinity College, Cambridge / On 15 September 1940, all England stood on alert / Many expected the German invasion would come any day / Shortly after three in the afternoon / A large formation of German bombers / Was attacked in the skies above this spot / By the Spitfires of 603 Squadron // While pressing his attack Peter Pease was struck / By cannon fire of an enemy fighter / He fell in flames in the field southeast of this spot / His last act was to rev his engine to avoid nearby houses / A tree now stands where he fell // (image) / Doubt not that in this lonely field was laid / A heart once pregnant with celestial fire; / Hands that the rod of empire might have swayed, ‘ Or waked to ecstasy the living lyre. // In loving memory / Some of the many / Honour this one of the few / 15 September 2015 / Battle of Britain Day
